key_insight: IQ-JEPA learns tissue sound speed and attenuation from ultrasound IQ data by first self-supervising on unlabeled channel data to predict masked latent regions, then fine-tuning on a small labeled simulation set.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for expensive labeled ultrasound simulations and improves label efficiency for quantitative ultrasound workflows that need fast, accurate sound-speed estimation.
method: Pretrain a joint-embedding predictive encoder on unlabeled complex IQ data by predicting masked-region representations from visible context.
Use a Hermitian Vision Transformer that operates directly on complex-valued IQ signals with phase-equivariant attention and phase-invariant feed-forward operations.
Fine-tune the pretrained encoder on simulated sound-speed maps and transfer the frozen features to sound speed and attenuation tasks.
evidence_signal: On 79,293 Fullwave 2.5 simulations, pretraining with 63,435 unlabeled acquisitions achieved 15.60 m/s error at 10,000 labels and 8.71 m/s at full labels, outperforming supervised training in label efficiency.
watch_item: Performance still depends on simulation quality and may transfer less cleanly across acquisition settings, so real-world validation and robustness checks are important.
paper_title: IQ-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with a Hermitian Vision Transformer for Sound Speed and Attenuation Estimation from Ultrasound IQ Data
